camb-002.title: The Cambrian explosion
camb-002.text:
In about 20–25 million years, life went from a handful of body plans to nearly all of today's. Beginning about 538.8 Ma, complex life diversified suddenly and produced the first representatives of most modern animal phyla. This is the Cambrian explosion. Its rate of diversification is unmatched among marine animals, though how explosive it really was is still debated.

Animals changed in every way at once. They gained mineralized skeletons, more complex bodies and more complex behavior. They began to burrow, churning the sea floor and opening new ecosystems below it.

Oxygen may have lit the fuse. Molybdenum isotopes tie rising early Cambrian biodiversity to the spread of oxygenated bottom waters, which supports oxygen as a driver. The burst did not last forever. Its high evolutionary rates had ended by 521 Ma, when {{ref:camb-028}}.
